name: Clanbook: Malkavian - New Derangements, Network Powers, Merits and Flaws

text.content:
These supplement the core @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference-st.JournalEntry.yEPxZHRgMGIQ2JJQ]{Derangements} list (see the Derangements journal) with additional options drawn from Clanbook: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian}, meant to flesh out convincing Lunatics beyond the baseline set. As with all Derangements, take these only with Storyteller consultation.

  • Desensitization: A virtual emotional amputee, unable to make the connections needed to feel joy, sadness, anger or love, even under supernatural compulsion such as Dominate or the blood bond — the character goes through the motions without real investment. Frenzy manifests as chillingly silent violence; Rötschreck as a silent, instinctive flight. Mechanically, the character suffers a one-Trait penalty to Social challenges requiring genuine warmth or emotion, cannot purchase Performance, and faces +2 difficulty on any Humanity/Path Virtue (Conscience/Conviction) test.
  • Disassociative Blood-Spending: The character unconsciously spends Blood Traits/points at inappropriate times without meaning to — boosting Physical Traits mid-conversation, or waking up a Blood Trait short with no memory of why. Once per session, the Storyteller may simply inform the player that the character is missing a Blood Trait without further explanation.
  • Masochism: The character associates pain with pleasure, typically tied to feeding, and feels shame or self-disgust at the act of drinking blood, resolving it only through suffering. Once wounded past a light injury, the character must win a Willpower test or lose her next action reveling in the pain; healing wounds with blood requires a further, difficult Self-Control test.
  • Memory Lapses: Minor, escalating memory loss the player can ad-lib in small ways, but which the Storyteller should periodically make dramatically significant (forgetting how to use a familiar Ability or skill for a scene). Requires Storyteller buy-in before play, since overuse can wreck other players' trust in the character's reliability.
  • Power-Object Fixation: The character has invested her self-confidence in an external object (an heirloom, a weapon, a keepsake) tied to a past trauma, and cannot function properly without it — a two-Trait penalty to all challenges while separated from it, and a Willpower test to avoid visibly, compulsively seeking comfort from the object under stress. Can spawn related derangements (such as an abuse victim developing her abuser's mannerisms) over time.
  • Self-Annihilation Impulse: An unconscious death wish, more common in older vampires, triggered by direct confrontation with the character's own immortality (visiting a mortal descendant's grave, watching a ghoul die of old age). A failed Willpower test sends the character on an unconscious, dangerous, Masquerade-risking errand for the rest of the scene that she will doggedly pursue and rationalize as safe.
  • Synesthesia: The character's senses are scrambled — she "hears" colors, "tastes" sounds, and the like — making everyday communication difficult ("cut the sandpapery wire" instead of "cut the red wire"). Two-Trait penalty to Expression/Performance challenges outside of surreal art; a Willpower Trait can be spent to translate sensory input into normal terms for a scene.

Note: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.derangements.JournalEntry.2ba8fe249a2b4400]{Regression} and Multiple Personality Disorder variants of these same ideas already exist in the core Derangements list; the Clanbook material above is presented as additional, distinct options rather than replacements.

Only a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} can deliberately send the Call, the wordless psychic summons that draws the clan to a gathering. It conveys no verbal content, only an impression of a place and a time — strong enough that even a Malkavian with no local language skill could follow it to a gathering point in a foreign city.

MET System: Sending the Call requires the character to announce her intent to a Storyteller, who then notifies the various Malkavian characters in play as appropriate (a good practice is flagging affected character sheets a few days ahead of a session). Success sending the Call is treated as automatic, but a character cannot reach beyond her own city's limits — a Call that crosses city lines is best kept as a Storyteller-controlled plot device rather than a player-triggered effect. Whether an individual Malkavian actually notices and responds to a Call depends on her own connection to the Madness Network (see Malkavian Time, in @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.cb34d85fb87945f4]{Malkavian Society: The Madness Network and Clan Practices}).

An elder @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} power letting a Lunatic deliberately quest into the clan's shared "Legion-mind" for the answer to a specific question, drawing on whatever some Malkavian somewhere (excluding Malkav himself) might know.

MET System: The player expends one or more Mental Traits (more Traits spent yields a more precise answer, at Storyteller discretion) and makes a simple test. On a win or tie, the character taps the Cobweb successfully and receives the information sought, filtered through the Storyteller's judgment of what's plausible for the clan to "know." On a loss, the character is instead flooded with the Network's ambient madness and gains two additional temporary @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference-st.JournalEntry.yEPxZHRgMGIQ2JJQ]{Derangements} for the next hour or scene (drawing from a prepared derangement-card pool is a fast way to adjudicate this). Without a Storyteller available to narrate the effect directly, an alternate fast resolution lets a character spend two Mental Traits and make the same test to temporarily gain one extra level of a Lore Ability she already has some rating in (e.g. Noddist Lore 2 becomes Noddist Lore 3 for one use), subject to Storyteller approval.

An Obfuscate-linked power that lets a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} encode a hidden message inside irrational-looking writing (graffiti, ravings scrawled on a cell wall) that reads as gibberish to anyone outside the clan, but which another Malkavian can decode simply by reading it. A writer can address a message to the whole clan or to one specific Malkavian she personally knows (or knows the sire or a childe of). Non-Malkavians with sufficiently advanced Auspex can attempt to crack a Scrawl, but a failed attempt risks inflicting a temporary derangement on the would-be decoder as her own mind supplies the wrong pattern.

MET System: This power is difficult to run live without abusing player trust. A workable approach is a physical "Scrawl" card (a distinct color of index card works well) left at the scene, blank-fronted with the hidden note on the back, honor-system-restricted to Malkavian readers; a more secure but slower method has the card direct the finder to see a Storyteller in person. Storytellers should feel free to restrict Scrawl to downtime/between-session use, or disallow it outright, if it bogs down live play.

• Immaculate Aura (1-Trait Merit): The character's aura never betrays her insanity, remaining steady even while frenzied, in Rötschreck, or in the grip of a derangement.
  • Benevolent Blood (1-Trait Merit): The character's vitae carries a lessened Curse of Malkav. Ghouls she creates never gain derangements from drinking her blood, no matter how much they're fed, though any childe she Embraces still gains a derangement as usual — the Curse survives dilution in the Embrace even when it doesn't in ghouled mortal blood.
  • Sympathetic Bond (5-Trait Merit): An unconscious supernatural feedback runs through the character's blood bonds. Any regnant who binds this character also becomes equally bound to her in return, even if that regnant was already bound elsewhere — a recipe for tangled, involuntary polyamorous blood ties.
  • Stigmata (2- or 4-Trait Flaw): The character constantly weeps blood from phantom wounds, costing an extra Blood Trait every evening just before dawn. The 2-Trait version (visible palms or similar) imposes a one-Trait penalty on Social challenges; the 4-Trait version (bleeding from the eye sockets) imposes a two-Trait penalty on Social challenges and a further one-Trait penalty on visual Perception challenges, and makes passing among mortals extremely difficult.
  • Infectious (3-Trait Flaw): The character's bite spreads clan madness to mortals. Every three Blood Traits drawn from a mortal during feeding inflicts one temporary Derangement on the victim, lasting roughly a week — Malkavians with this Flaw are disproportionately drawn to feeding quietly in asylums, where a little more madness goes unnoticed.

The core rulebook's Mental Flaws, along with Acute Sense, Infamous Sire, Medium, Oracular Ability, Cursed, Eerie Presence and Grip of the Damned, remain particularly apt choices for @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} characters even though they are not clan-exclusive.

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Malkavian, Chapter Two - Inside Bedlam
